tagline: A copper road follows the Ocoee past dams and Olympic whitewater.
intro: The Ocoee Scenic Byway winds past Parksville Lake and the rocky bluffs of the Ocoee River Gorge in Cherokee National Forest. Most of the river route is two lanes, with a short four-lane stretch west of the Whitewater Center. Designated in July 1988, it was the nation’s first National Forest Scenic Byway. The Forest Service highlights the gorge and the Chilhowee Scenic Spur’s views across the Tennessee Valley to the Cumberland Mountains and Georgia’s mountains.

The route follows the Old Copper Road, a wagon route used in the 1850s to carry copper from the Copper Basin to Cleveland and Chattanooga. US 64 through the gorge was built around 1926 and paved in the 1940s. The road changed again for the 1996 Olympics, when part of a four-lane section was narrowed to make room for spectator stands.

Travel east from Parksville Lake, where US 64 passes just north of Ocoee Dam No. 1. Forest Road 77 branches into the seven-mile Chilhowee Scenic Spur, climbing to the Chilhowee Mountains. Back on the river route, continue through the gorge to the Whitewater Center near Ducktown. Ducktown lies in the Copper Basin, where copper mining ran from 1847 to 1987.

moments.title: Parksville Lake
moments.text: Parksville Lake spreads behind Ocoee Dam No. 1 where the river leaves the Appalachian Mountains for the Tennessee Valley. Completed in 1911, the dam was one of Tennessee’s first hydroelectric projects. The Eastern Tennessee Power Company built it as Chattanooga’s growing industries demanded more electricity. Commercial operation began in January 1912. US 64 passes north of the dam; the reservoir extends east up the Ocoee and south along Baker Creek. The dam is 135 feet high and 840 feet long. Its concrete arched spillway forms part of a power project now owned by the Tennessee Valley Authority.

moments.title: Chilhowee Scenic Spur
moments.text: Forest Road 77 leaves the river route for a seven-mile climb to the Chilhowee Mountains. The spur leads to Chilhowee Recreation Area, with overlooks offering views of the Tennessee Valley, Cumberland Mountains and mountains in Georgia. The Forest Service identifies several overlooks with places for a picnic or short hike.
moments.notice: Overlooks take in the Tennessee Valley, Cumberland Mountains and mountains in Georgia.

moments.title: Ocoee Whitewater Center
moments.text: The 1996 Olympic canoe slalom course was made by narrowing a 1,640-foot stretch of the Upper Ocoee by two-thirds. Rock-covered levees reduced the river’s width from 200 feet to 70 feet, creating the required drops and eddies. Water diverted for power generation normally leaves this reach dry except during releases. The visitor center’s main building was destroyed by fire on April 26, 2022. The day-use area reopened on May 27, 2023. Before construction, engineers tested the proposed river changes in a water-filled model built at one-tenth scale near Ocoee Dam No. 1.
